description: Little helper to run CNCF's k3s in Docker

summary.one_liner: k3d is a command-line tool that runs lightweight k3s Kubernetes clusters inside Docker containers, letting you spin up multi-node clusters on a single machine.
summary.what_it_does: k3d creates containerized k3s clusters, so a multi-node k3s cluster can run on one machine using Docker. Each cluster is created with a single command, such as `k3d cluster create CLUSTER_NAME`, which starts one k3s server container plus a loadbalancer container. The tool can merge the new cluster into your default kubeconfig and switch the current context to it. Clusters are removed with `k3d cluster delete`. The README also covers building from source with make, installing via install script, Homebrew, MacPorts, AUR, Chocolatey, Scoop, or go install, and points to k3d.io for full documentation.
use_cases: spin up a local multi-node Kubernetes cluster for development
test Kubernetes manifests without a cloud account
run k3s clusters on a single laptop or workstation
create throwaway clusters for CI or integration tests
experiment with kubectl against a disposable cluster
notable: Runs multi-node k3s clusters on one machine by using Docker containers as cluster nodes
Creates a single-node cluster with a loadbalancer container in one command
Can merge the new cluster into your kubeconfig and switch context automatically
Community-driven project, originally derived from zeerorg's k3s-in-docker and later reimplemented in Go
Available through many package managers across macOS, Linux and Windows
caveats: Requires Docker; k3d v5.x.x needs at least Docker v20.10.5 (runc >= v1.0.0-rc93)
Installing via go install gives unreleased, bleeding-edge changes
Community-driven project and not an official Rancher (SUSE) product; relies on sponsorships for significant work
